criteria.description: PayPal loopback stub, fake webhook signer and the shared PaymentProvider contract suite (test-engineer owned)
criteria.notes: The e0 plan command passes 160/160, including the reference adapter and the leaky negative control. In my e1 run, the suite runs against the fake and the Sandbox adapter (216 tests, 209 pass, 7 skipped by design: the fake has no OAuth or wire). The stub's approval page sends one CSP. The stub's interpretations (submission delta 19) are acceptable; they are the spec's guesses and stay LIVE-DEPENDENT (LIVE-P1, OQ-D5).

criteria.description: Payment adapters: DB-backed fake with faults and replay model, fake approval listener with its own CSP, Sandbox REST v2 adapter (stub-verified), merchant mapping
criteria.notes:
The e1 plan command passes 487/480/7 skipped by design.

What I checked in the code:
- The Sandbox adapter sends paypal-request-id = requestId on every call that carries one (sandbox.js L169), and checkArguments refuses a mutating call without a well-formed requestId before anything is sent (provider.js L76). One AbortSignal covers OAuth and the call.
- The fake runs each call in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE: fault, replay by (merchant_key, request_id), effect, then a fake_paypal_calls row.

What my runs show:
- Mutant M18 (listener CSP form-action without the app origin) is killed by the browser journey (2/2 red).
- The TR-R4-3 probe counted 2019 entries into the fake and Sandbox provider methods across the suites, none inside a transaction.

The fake and stub interpretations (deltas 18, 19, 20) are acceptable. The adapter remains unverified against real PayPal (LIVE-P1, LIVE-P2).

criteria.description: Provider call protocol and payment flow: paypal/create, return and cancel handlers, abandon, void rule with the resolution hook, order presentation and receipt
criteria.notes:
The e2 plan command passes 92/92.

The protocol matches spec section 2-4:
- Start is its own transaction with CAS status = 'intent' AND started_at IS NULL, and status = 'unknown' AND send_token IS NULL only for a caller that resolved the call (L139-L147).
- Send happens outside any transaction under a deadline of the timeout + 1 s (L370).
- Record is a CAS on id, send_token and status 'intent', with the mapped transition and an optional fence in the same transaction. Zero rows log provider.result_fenced.
- Every sender passes requestId = call.operation_key (L318-L326). The capture sender in saga.js does the same.

Mutants killed:
- M1: create amount from the operation row (2 RS-19 tests red);
- M5: start CAS without started_at (the protocol unit test red);
- M11: in-flight authorize voided locally;
- M12: no provider void queued (20 red);
- M13: the resolution hook removed from the authorize record.

The return handler's steps 1-6 match the spec. A foreign token is 404 before any provider call.

SEC-E-2 (TR-E-2, minor) concerns the return route's provider reads and rides an e2 reset with TR-E-1. Its acceptance criteria are otherwise met.

criteria.description: Verified PayPal webhooks: pre-checks, per-IP limit, signature verification, dedupe among valid events, merchant-scoped mapping
Execute claim and capture saga (steps 1-4) with lease fencing, and the reconciler (stale intents, read-before-resend, pending polls, expiry, sender table, housekeeping)
Payment UI: approvals per supplier with provider badges, try-again and abandon, complete purchase, receipt, supplier ready/handover, cancelled presentation, polling
criteria.notes:
The e5 plan command passes 166/166, and the browser suite is 10/10 on the final tree.

returnNoticeModel follows the state (waiting / confirmed / absent). I looked at the 360 px final screenshot: receipt recorded, status 'Purchase confirmed', simulated badges.

The UI shows nothing for paypal=not_approved or check_failed (delta 6). This is an info UX note for f3 (TR-E-6). Assumption 1 is not delivered, and the fallback works (FU-39). The fixture title is FU-38.

criteria.description: Two-process execute test, HTTP contract extension, opt-in live PayPal suite files, and the cross-site happy-path browser journey
criteria.notes:
The e6 plan command passes: npm test 2087/2079/0 fail/8 skipped, then the browser suite 10/10.

RS-20 two-process test:
- it asserts exactly 2N provider calls (N get_authorization + N capture), none replayed, all from the winner's pid, reads before captures, keys so:<id>:capture:1, and N fake captures;
- my M17 (the saga sends a second capture under a new request id) turns both rounds red, so the test would fail on a second capture.

The contract table has 52 NFR6 scenarios and 0 skipped rows. 'Every route of the table is registered' and 'every registered route has a scenario' are green.

The journey is cross-site: it asserts the app on localhost, the approval page on 127.0.0.1, waitForURL on the app origin, and exactly one GET return/cancel per action. My M18 (CSP form-action without the app origin) turns both widths red, so the CSP assertion bites.

The log line's userId check in the shared helper is conditional (L99): TR-E-3, minor.

The live files refuse per file (NFR3 tests in my npm test run).

criteria.description: The PaymentProvider contract with a DB-backed fake (faults, PayPal-Request-Id replay model, fake approval listener on a different site with its own CSP) and the Sandbox REST v2 adapter verified against a loopback paypal-stub; the provider call protocol with the sender table; create/return/cancel/abandon with the void rule; the execute claim and captures with lease fencing; the reconciler (stale intents, read-before-resend, pending polls, expiry); verified webhooks; the payment UI; and the two-process execute and browser happy-path journeys.
criteria.notes:
RS-04 (create half), RS-18, RS-19, RS-20, RS-21, RS-23, RS-24, RS-25, RS-27 (payment half) and RS-31(a) are each proved by the named tests, green in my runs, against the fake or the stub only. ARCH-22, ARCH-23, F-TR-3, F-TR-11, SEC-3 and the contract suite on both adapters are likewise covered. LIVE-P1, LIVE-P2 and OQ-D5 are correctly not claimed. Artifact coverage is exact.

Not met as a whole, because 'verified webhooks' and the spec's mapping are violated (TR-E-1, major). Through it, a genuine late event both loses a purchase and bypasses the read-before-resend layer of the saga.

No phase E task designs or changes a hook, a guard or root discovery, so its 'Applies when' list does not hold, and the stated reasons are true. findings.title: (= SEC-E-1) A late, validly signed PAYMENT.AUTHORIZATION.CREATED moves capture_pending and unknown(prev authorized|capture_pending) back to authorized: a pending purchase is compensated, and an unknown capture is re-sent without a read
findings.detail:
Where:
- src/services/webhooks.js L54 maps 'PAYMENT.AUTHORIZATION.CREATED' to target 'authorized' with no `from` list.
- L261-L264 then admit every edge into authorized that the payment table allows. That includes capture_pending -> authorized (an edge that exists for CAPTURE.DENIED) and unknown -> authorized when prev_status is authorized or capture_pending (effective === target, or canTransition(capture_pending, authorized)).
- The spec maps this event 'pending -> authorized' (spec Webhooks, events list).
- e3's mapping table (test/api/webhooks.test.js L521-L527) has rows for authorization_pending, approved, unknown(prev approved), authorized, voided, created and unknown(prev refund_pending). It has none for capture_pending or unknown(prev authorized), so no test notices.

My reproduction (ev:ev-mv3wp57z-01f9ce7d, which passes when the defect is observed):
- P1: fault capture_pending on A, then execute. A is capture_pending. A signed late AUTHORIZATION.CREATED is answered 200 applied, and A becomes authorized. Over the next ticks the plan is taken over and compensated (non_executable CAPTURE_FAILED): A's void is refused because a capture is pending, resolveRejectedVoid puts A back in capture_pending, and B is voided. When the provider completes A's capture, A is captured and then refunded: the buyer is charged and refunded, and the purchase is lost.
- P2: fault lost_response:capture on A, so A is unknown(prev authorized) with the capture applied. The late event moves A to authorized, while the capture call stays unknown. With get_authorization and get_order failing (http 500), the next tick takes the plan over and the saga re-sends capture:1 with no successful read. Only the fake's PayPal-Request-Id replay prevents a second capture (capture:A:replayed).
- Security reproduced both (W-ORDER S2, S3; ev:ev-mv3w48uy-0190adfa, a reproduction run).

Money was neither lost nor doubled in any run. Layer 3 of 'why no double capture' (read before any re-send, spec Payment saga step 6) is bypassed, leaving layers 4-5, which are LIVE-DEPENDENT for the Sandbox (request-id retention, final_capture). PayPal does deliver events late and out of order: it retries for days, and this route answers 503 whenever verification is unreachable.
findings.recommendation:
Owner: backend-engineer, through an e3 reset inside this phase (webhooks.js and webhooks.test.js are e3's).

Resolved when all of these hold:
1. PAYMENT.AUTHORIZATION.CREATED gets from: ['approved', 'authorization_pending']. 'approved' stays because the event can beat the return handler's own answer. The existing effective = prev_status rule keeps unknown(prev approved | authorization_pending) resolving.
2. capture_pending, unknown(prev authorized), unknown(prev capture_pending) and every other origin are answered 200 flagged TRANSITION_NOT_ALLOWED, with no column change and no audit.
3. The e3 mapping table gains those three rows, named after this finding.
4. My probe tr-probe-webhook-order.test.js and security's W-ORDER are re-run unchanged, and their P1/P2 and S2/S3 'OBSERVED'/REPRO assertions now fail. S1 and S4 still pass.
5. The e3 plan command, npm test and npm run test:browser are green.

The defence in depth for saga.js is TR-E-4 (f2).

findings.title: (= SEC-E-2) GET /api/paypal/return is public, so the 300/min user limit does not apply: every hit on an unapproved order is one provider getOrder with the merchant's credentials
findings.detail:
src/routes/paypal.js registers return with policy public. The general limiter is not applied to public routes. payments.js L200 calls getOrder on every hit while the operation is created.

Security's reproduction (ev:ev-mv3wkmdf-014def88): 400 hits within one minute gave 400 getOrder calls and no 429, while 400 paypal/create calls are cut at 300.

Impact: availability, not money or data. In single-credential mode one account can spend the shared PayPal app's rate budget, and other buyers then see retryable/503.
findings.recommendation:
Owner: backend-engineer, through an e2 reset dispatched with TR-E-1 (routes/paypal.js and services/payments.js are e2's).

Resolved when a test shows the return route bounded per identified user, with the anonymous redirect, the 404 for a foreign token, the RS-20 three-hit and the crash-hook tests unchanged. Either:
- apply the general limiter after ctx.auth.identify; or
- allow at most one getOrder per operation per few seconds, answering paypal=check_failed otherwise.

If the orchestrator decides not to dispatch e2, record an acceptance decision naming the residual. It must not ride into delivery silently.

findings.title: The shared approval round-trip helper accepts a GET /api/paypal/return log line without userId, so the plan's 'with the session's user id in the server log' clause is not enforced by the browser journey
findings.detail:
test/browser/helpers/approval-roundtrip.js L99 reads `if (entry.userId !== undefined) assert.equal(entry.userId, userId, ...)`. A regression of the e4-reset log fix (src/app.js L211-L214) would leave journey-happy green.

Today the line does carry userId 9 at both widths (my browser run), and the API test execute.test.js L701 pins the log line, so this is a test-strength issue, not a defect. The e6 handoff says the check 'tightens by itself'; it does not, because an absent field still passes. f4 and g3 reuse this helper.
findings.recommendation:
Owner: test-engineer. In an e6 reset if one is dispatched this round; otherwise f4, which owns test/browser/helpers/** and is the next reuser, by recorded follow-up.

Resolved when the helper asserts entry.userId === userId unconditionally, and a scratch negative control (the app.js finally-block copy removed) turns journey-happy red at both widths.

findings.title: Mutant M6 survives: the F-TR-7 pause guard inside captureLoop (saga.js L531) is untested; the saga also re-sends an unknown capture relying on the reconciler's earlier read (SEC-E-1 recommendation 5)
findings.detail:
From my first mutant run (ev:ev-mv3wo4q9-014c6847, which fails by design because my driver fails on any survivor): replacing the condition at saga.js L531 with false leaves the e4 suite 71/71 green.

The rule is pinned elsewhere:
- the takeover exclusion: M7 is killed (ev:ev-mv3xewar-0170b19e);
- the pause after a PENDING or unknown answer (L566).

So L531 is defence in depth that matters only when an operation changes between the takeover and the run, for example through a webhook or a second process.

Related: captureLoop treats an authorized operation with an unknown, token-less capture call as resendable (L552, L559) without its own read. Spec step 6 says the new holder reads before any send. Today that is safe only because step 2 of the same tick read first, and TR-E-1 is the path that breaks it.
findings.recommendation:
Owner: f2-compensation-takeover-admin (owns saga.js), by follow-up.
- (a) Before re-sending an unknown capture call in captureLoop, read the authorization under the lease, as spec step 6 says.
- (b) Add a test where an operation becomes capture_pending or unknown after the takeover and before the resumed run; it must pause and send nothing. M6 must then be killed.
This is not a condition of this gate.

findings.title: Mutant M2 survives: no test pins the capture (or refund) amount to supplier_orders.total_cents when payment_operations.amount_cents disagrees
findings.detail:
Taking the capture amount from payment_operations.amount_cents instead of supplier_orders.total_cents leaves 78/78 green (ev:ev-mv3wo4q9-014c6847). M2b (+1 cent) is killed (31 red).

The mutant is equivalent in practice. amount_cents is written once, at reservation, equal to the order total (reservations.js L177), and is never updated. total_cents is never updated either (security AMT-3). Refunds use amount_cents (calls.js L326).

The RS-19 test pins only create_order against a disagreeing row (amount-tampering.test.js L106).
findings.recommendation: Optional, for f2 (capture-compensation.test.js): assert the capture and refund request amounts against supplier_orders.total_cents with a disagreeing operation row, or document that the two columns are equal by construction. The verification report lists it with delta 24 (TR-E-6).

findings.title: Contract deltas 1-21 judged acceptable; four unlisted deltas (22-25) to add to the verification report
findings.recommendation: Owner: delivery-lead. Add 22-25 to verification-report item 10. Optional for f3: a neutral notice for not_approved/check_failed ('PayPal did not confirm the approval; try again').

findings.title: Security info items SEC-E-I1..I5 folded
findings.detail:
- SEC-E-I1: the fake's and the stub's webhook signatures are not merchant-bound. Offline this is contained by the global dedupe and SEC-16 scoping; it is LIVE-DEPENDENT for PayPal.
- SEC-E-I2: a forged body under a seen transmission id gets 200 duplicate with no effect. Accepted.
- SEC-E-I3: an expired authorization cannot be voided and escalates with void_failed (remaining issue 9, f2).
- SEC-E-I4: the FU-34 one-tick window shows no loss or doubling (ev:ev-mv3wifuf-01eb0c2d), so dec-mv3vuigy-0109feb6 is accepted by both reviewers.
- SEC-E-I5: the return handler can authorize before the expiry pass, and the next pass voids it.
findings.recommendation:
Owners:
- I1: g2/g3, adding merchantKey to the fake's signing string, or listing it as LIVE-P1;
- I3: f2, treating EXPIRED read back after a rejected void as settled.
I2, I4 and I5 need no action. delivery-lead carries them to the verification report.

findings.title: Tests-after-code disclosure (e1-e4) and the engineers' scratch mutation proofs without evidence ids: my own recorded mutants suffice for the money paths
findings.recommendation: Nothing further for this gate. For the e2/e3 resets of this round: record the red-first run of each new test through evidence run before the fix, so that the new rows carry their own proof.
